mods.description: Talk to Claude Code from Minecraft chat. Claude can build, run commands, design custom items, and act in the world through an embedded MCP server.

releases.notes:
Effects can now follow a player or mob around, and return portals break like nether portals.

## What's new
- **Effects that follow.** Claude can attach an effect to a player or creature: an aura around you, a rain cloud over someone's head, a mob wreathed in flames. It moves with them until it ends or they die, and any `field` (pulling or pushing mobs) moves along too.
  - Particles travel with the effect, or stay where they appeared for trails and footprints.
  - In commands: `/claude effect <id> on <targets> [height]`, so items and creatures can use it too (for example `claude effect aura on @s` in an item's `use_commands`).
- **Return portals break like nether portals.** The portal built on the far side of your first trip now loses all its panes if you break a frame block or any pane. Portals you build yourself are left alone.
- **Thinner portals.** Claude now makes portal blocks pane-thin like vanilla's, not full blocks.

Your `system-prompt.md` updates automatically unless you've edited it. Your edits are never overwritten.

## Requirements
Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.20.1+, Fabric API, Java 25, and Claude Code on the host. **Every player** needs this jar and Fabric API. Remove `claudecraft-0.14.0.jar` from your mods folder when you install this one.

releases.notes:
Claude can now design real particle effects whose look and motion it decides: smoke, dust, fire, debris, rain, leaves and magic. Effects also stay visible from much farther away.

## What's new
- **Particle effects.** Effects get a new `particles` part, so a campfire can have rising smoke, a spell can leave a trail of glowing motes, and a storm can swirl and throw debris, instead of everything being glowing sparks.
  - Claude picks the look: any vanilla particle sprite (smoke, gusts, flames, sparks, leaves, souls and more, animated) or chips of a block's texture, with colors and sizes that change over each particle's life.
  - Claude designs the motion: where particles appear, how fast they start, gravity, drag and spin, plus a flow field that keeps pushing them, for swirls, vortices, updrafts and orbits.
  - They work anywhere effects already play: weapons, projectile trails, hit effects, creature attacks, `/claude effect` and `/summon custom:<id>`, and they combine with a `field` that pulls or pushes mobs.
- **Effects visible from afar.** Beams, lightning, orbs and other effects used to vanish about 16 blocks away. They now show at any distance your game has the area loaded.
- **Vanilla particles reach further.** Claude now adds `force` to `/particle` commands, which otherwise only show within 32 blocks.

Your `system-prompt.md` updates automatically unless you've edited it. Your edits are never overwritten.

mods.description: Talk to Claude Code from Minecraft chat. Claude can build, run commands, design custom items, and act in the world through an embedded MCP server.

releases.notes:
Claude can now work on more than one request at a time. Friends can also bring their own Claude to your world instead of using yours.

## What's new
- **Two sessions at once.** By default Claude works on two requests in parallel. Each is its own conversation: a player's follow-ups stay with the session handling them, and a new request goes to an idle one instead of waiting.
  - The status line shows every working session, labeled by player: `✻ Alex: Surveying… · Sam: Building…`.
  - Each session gets its own undo steps, so `/claude undo` never mixes two people's builds.
- **Friends can use their own Claude.** A friend can run Claude on their own computer, with their own Claude Code account, while building in your world.
  - Their replies show in chat as `[Name's Claude]`. `/claude stop`, `/claude reset` and `/claude status` include them.
  - Everything goes over the normal Minecraft connection, so it works with Essential, LAN or a server, with no port forwarding.
  - `view_build` pictures of places your friend's game already has loaded are drawn on their computer. Anything else comes from the host.
- **ClaudeCraft menu.** The new **ClaudeCraft…** button in the corner of the pause menu opens a menu for:
  - how many sessions run at once (1–8)
  - whether friends can use their own Claude
  - whether you use your own

  Changes apply right away and are saved. Only the host or an operator can change the world's settings.

## Config
- `maxConcurrentSessions` (default `2`): how many requests Claude works on at once. `1` gives the old one-at-a-time behavior.
- `allowPlayerClaude` (default `false`): host setting. Lets players on `allowedPlayers` use their own Claude.
- `useOwnClaude` (default `false`): player setting. Use your own Claude when joining someone else's world.

All three can also be set from the ClaudeCraft menu. Your `system-prompt.md` updates automatically unless you've edited it. Your edits are never overwritten.

## Good to know
- When a friend's own Claude is allowed, it can change your world through the same tools as yours, including commands at your `commandPermissionLevel`. Only turn it on for people you'd let use your Claude.
- Sessions don't share conversations. One only knows about another's work by looking at the world.

## Requirements
Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.20.1+, Fabric API, Java 25, and Claude Code on the host (and on any friend using their own Claude). **Every player** needs this jar and Fabric API. Remove `claudecraft-0.12.0.jar` from your mods folder when you install this one.

releases.notes:
Claude can now design animated blocks: flickering fire that sets you alight, shimmering portals you can step through to its dimensions, flowing lava, pulsing machines.

## What's new
- **Animated blocks** (`define_block`):
  - **Color cycling:** a palette color can be a list that the block steps through. Letters cycling the same colors from different starting points make swirls and flowing bands, like a nether portal.
  - **Frames:** whole drawings to step through, for things whose shape changes, like flames. `frame_time` sets the speed, and `desync` starts each block at a different point so a field of fire doesn't flicker in step.
  - **Cross shape:** a picture drawn on two crossed diagonal planes, like vanilla fire and flowers.
  - Animated blocks move in your hand and inventory too.
- **Livelier blocks:**
  - `glow`: full brightness in the dark, like lava.
  - `particles`: flame, smoke, portal, dust in any color, and more.
  - `ambient_sound`: a crackle or hum now and then.
  - `burns`: sets anything inside on fire, like vanilla fire.
  - `inside_commands`: runs commands on whatever stands in the block.
- **Portals.** A block with `portal` works like a nether portal: stand in it (a few seconds in survival, instantly in creative) and it takes you to its dimension, or back to the overworld from there. The first trip builds a copy of the portal and its frame on the far side, so there's always a way home. Mobs and items can go through too.

## Good to know
- Only the moving parts of an animated block are redrawn each frame, and only within 128 blocks.
- Moving parts get flat lighting, without the soft corner shadows of smooth lighting. It's barely noticeable on glowing blocks.

## Config
No new options. Your `system-prompt.md` updates automatically unless you've edited it. Your edits are never overwritten.

## Requirements
Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.20.1+, Fabric API, Java 25, and Claude Code on the host. **Every player** needs this jar and Fabric API. Remove `claudecraft-0.11.0.jar` from your mods folder when you install this one.

releases.notes:
Claude can now design real visual effects: glowing lasers, crackling lightning, black holes, shockwaves. Ask for a lightning gun or a black hole gun and get one that looks the part.

## What's new
- **Custom effects** (`define_effect`). Claude builds an effect from parts, and every player's game draws it:
  - **Beams:** straight lasers, crackling lightning that forks and re-crackles, flowing waves and spirals.
  - **Orbs:** a solid body (even pure black), a soft halo and a spinning ring, like a black hole's accretion disk.
  - **Shockwaves:** rings that expand along the ground or facing outward.
  - **Sparks:** sparks that burst out, drift along a beam or swirl inward.
  - Glows blend like light, and effects can play a sound.
- **Fields.** An effect can pull things toward it or push them away, and hurt what's inside, so a black hole really sucks mobs in.
- **Effect weapons.** Items can fire instant beams that hit the first thing in their path, like a laser or lightning gun. Thrown items can glow and trail an effect as they fly, and any shot can set off an effect where it lands. Creatures' ranged attacks work the same way, so a dragon can breathe lightning.
- **Effects in commands.** `/claude effect <id> <from> [to]` and `/summon custom:<id>`, so blocks, creature abilities and other commands can trigger effects too.

## Good to know
- Effects don't light up the world, and a field still going when you close the world won't be there when you reopen it.
- Claude can't see effects in its pictures, so it may ask you how one looks.

## Config
No new options. Your `system-prompt.md` updates automatically unless you've edited it. Your edits are never overwritten.

## Requirements
Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.20.1+, Fabric API, Java 25, and Claude Code on the host. **Every player** needs this jar and Fabric API. Remove `claudecraft-0.10.1.jar` from your mods folder when you install this one.

releases.notes:
A fix for the game running out of memory when lots of custom blocks sit next to each other.

## Fixes
- **Custom blocks now hide the faces next to them and block light, like stone.** Before, the game drew every hidden face of every custom block. A wall made of them was slow, and a dimension whose underground was a custom block could run the computer out of memory within seconds of arriving. See-through custom blocks (like custom glass) hide faces only against their own kind, and small shapes like lamps and chairs hide nothing.

## If you made a dimension with a custom block underground
Its chunks were generated while those blocks let light through, so caves may be lit oddly. Ask Claude to reset that dimension to regenerate it. This wipes anything built there.

## Requirements
Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.20.1+, Fabric API, Java 25, and Claude Code on the host. **Every player** needs this jar and Fabric API. Remove `claudecraft-0.10.0.jar` from your mods folder when you install this one.

releases.notes:
Claude can now create whole new dimensions while you play: a moon, an alien planet, floating sky islands, an endless cavern. They appear instantly, with no restart, and everyone can visit.

## What's new
- **Custom dimensions** (`define_dimension`). Claude picks:
  - **A sky:** daylight (sun, day and night, weather), cavern (a rock ceiling and dim light, like the Nether) or starry (an endless dark sky, like the End).
  - **A biome** for colors and life: any vanilla biome, or the new alien (purple sky, teal grass), crimson, frozen, toxic and golden.
  - **The terrain:** hills, mountains, flat, ocean, floating islands, caves or an empty void, with its height and roughness. It can be built from any blocks, including Claude's own custom blocks, or shaped with math for something stranger.
- **Visiting.** Claude can take players to any dimension and back, landing on safe ground: an air pocket in a cavern, or a small platform in the void. Portals are custom blocks that run `claude visit <dimension>` when stepped on.
- **Redesigning.** Asking for changes reshapes land generated from then on; Claude can also regenerate the whole dimension (after checking with you, since that wipes what's been built there).
- **Filling them.** Claude's creatures can live in a dimension's biome and its ores can generate there. Commands reach it as `custom:<id>`, e.g. `/execute in custom:moon run ...`.
- Dimensions are saved with the world and come back every time it's opened.

## Fixes
- Teleporting into a dimension no longer lands players on treetops.

## Config
No new options. Your `system-prompt.md` updates automatically unless you've edited it. Your edits are never overwritten.

## Requirements
Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.20.1+, Fabric API, Java 25, and Claude Code on the host. **Every player** needs this jar and Fabric API. Remove `claudecraft-0.9.0.jar` from your mods folder when you install this one.
